title: API documentation and GitHub Actions (Nirojan Selvanathan, 2019-2020)
description: Two Hall of Fame entries for one contributor. Most of the work lives outside the analysed repositories, so this story relies on the official pages, one commit, and the credits history.
narrative:
For a tool that many teams run from a build script, the documentation probably matters as much as the code. The Student Hall of Fame lists Nirojan Selvanathan for ZAP API documentation, GSoD, 2019 Autumn. The same listing gives a second entry for ZAP GitHub actions, a Direct entry in spring 2020.

The ZAP API documentation page has sections on exploring and attacking an application, getting results, authentication, advanced settings and an API catalogue. The repository README says it holds the source for that documentation, built with Slate. Neither page fetched mentions Season of Docs or names contributors, so the link to the 2019 entry rests on the Hall of Fame listing alone.

In February 2020 the only zaproxy commit under this author name added a check for Markdown report files to the Docker scripts. The credits history records him being promoted to the Core Team list that month and moved to the extended team in August 2021.

In April 2020 a blog post by him describes the ZAP Baseline action, a workflow with a daily cron trigger and a rules file that sets rules to WARN, FAIL, or IGNORE. In May 2020 a second post describes the ZAP full scan action, which runs the spider and an active scan and reports results as GitHub issues. A search of the zaproxy history found no commits for either action, so their code lies outside the repositories analysed here.

chapters.title: The two entries
chapters.text: The Student Hall of Fame lists Nirojan Selvanathan for "ZAP API documentation", GSoD, 2019 Autumn (blog, docs and repo links) and for "ZAP GitHub actions", Direct, 2020 Spring (two blog posts).

chapters.title: API documentation
chapters.text: The ZAP API documentation page at zaproxy.org/docs/api/ has sections on exploring and attacking an application, getting results, authentication, advanced settings, contributing, troubleshooting, and an API catalogue. The zaproxy/zap-api-docs repository README says it holds the source for that documentation, built with Slate. Neither page fetched mentions Season of Docs or names contributors, so the link to the 2019 entry rests on the Hall of Fame listing alone. The repository is not among the clones analysed here.

chapters.title: February 2020: one docker commit and the Core Team list
chapters.text: In zaproxy the only commit under this author name is "Adding missing check for markdown files (#5870)", dated 2020-02-21. It changes docker/zap-api-scan.py, docker/zap-baseline.py, docker/zap-full-scan.py and docker/CHANGELOG.md, adding report_md to the check for file-based options. In the credits page history in zap-core-help, "Promoted Nirojan :)" is dated 2020-02-28 and adds his entry to the Core Team list; "Move Nirojan to extended team" is dated 2021-08-06 and removes it from that list.

chapters.title: April and May 2020: the GitHub Actions blog posts
chapters.text: The blog post dated 2020-04-09, written by Nirojan Selvanathan, describes the ZAP Baseline action (zaproxy/action-baseline): a workflow with a daily cron trigger, issue tracking in GitHub issues, and a rules.tsv file to set rules to WARN, FAIL, or IGNORE. The post dated 2020-05-15, also by him, describes the ZAP full scan action, which runs the spider, an optional AJAX spider, and an active scan and reports results as GitHub issues. Both posts carry a notice that their content may be outdated. A search of the zaproxy history for "action-baseline" and "action-full-scan" found no commits, so the actions' own code is outside the analysed repositories.
